{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "ADISA is a newly created agency lacking experience with World Bank fiduciary requirements, creating high procurement and implementation risks.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated PMU staffed with experienced procurement and financial management specialists, supported by continuous capacity-building and Bank oversight.",
      "evidence": "ADISA is a newly-created agency and the PMU is not yet fully set up, the procurement risk rating is high."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "The ambitious and compressed reform timeline creates schedule pressure that could lead to implementation delays across multiple agencies.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Phase implementation across a five-year horizon, structure results-based financing incentives tied to DLIs through 2020, and provide targeted technical assistance.",
      "evidence": "The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk, which is mitigated by the project's span and incentives to deliver up to 2020."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Focusing heavily on digital e-services and centralized urban service centers risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and vulnerable populations with limited internet access.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish assisted digital access points, deploy non-digital information campaigns via grassroots groups, upgrade regional front offices, and monitor usage via user surveys.",
      "evidence": "risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Construction of the Citizen Service Center (CSC) building in Tirana may cause localized environmental impacts including dust, noise, waste, and worker safety hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce the Environmental Management Plan (EMP) as part of bidding and construction contracts, conduct regular site monitoring, and maintain regulatory permit compliance.",
      "evidence": "Potential environmental impacts that are associated with new construction include dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery on site"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Reforming administrative services across more than ten government agencies presents significant inter-agency coordination challenges.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Utilize governance bodies including the Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee, Project Steering Committee, and Prime Minister's Delivery Unit to align agency activities.",
      "evidence": "Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Civil servants and line agency managers may resist surrendering front-office responsibilities or changing entrenched administrative workflows.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy a dedicated change management and communication program, engage key reform champions early, and align institutional performance incentives.",
      "evidence": "Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Ongoing operation, maintenance, and software licensing costs for new IT systems and CSC facilities could impose long-term financial sustainability challenges.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate system lifecycle and maintenance costs into long-term budget planning, offset by operational efficiency gains achieved through business process re-engineering.",
      "evidence": "Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Incomplete legacy database digitization, missing ID numbers, and legal title disputes at IPRO could delay automated service delivery.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Re-engineer business processes, mandate National ID integration, and connect agency databases to the Government Interoperability Platform.",
      "evidence": "National ID number is missing for most records, only 45 to 50 percent of the archive is digitized, and legal issues over ownership remain"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Failure to complete global prerequisite DLI #5 (Reform Policy Document approval and baseline survey) would prevent all RBF loan disbursements.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize and fast-track the Reform Policy Document approval and baseline survey completion during project preparation using PPF funds.",
      "evidence": "This is a “global” DLI, which means that no disbursements under the RBF component will be made until DLI#5 is met."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Manual payroll systems and fragmented controls across participating agencies create risks of error in reporting Eligible Expenditure Programs (EEPs).",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct internal audits on payroll linkages, enforce dual signatures, and accelerate integration with the national HRMIS.",
      "evidence": "payroll systems remain by and large manual systems, and the associated controls are manually based as well. System cannot communicate with each other."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Inadequate financial management software and lack of donor-project experience at ADISA could cause delays in financial reporting and audit compliance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Recruit two finance specialists, procure dedicated accounting software during the PPF phase, and adopt a detailed Financial Management Manual.",
      "evidence": "Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations, therefore capacity strengthening would be recommended"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Failure to achieve and verify agreed Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) will result in withheld loan disbursements under the Results-Based Financing component.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted technical assistance for business process re-engineering, software deployment, and front-office upgrades, backed by third-party verification.",
      "evidence": "Where achievement of a DLI cannot be verified, an amount equivalent to the price of that DLI will be withheld."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: ADISA is a newly created agency lacking experience with World Bank fiduciary requirements, creating high procurement and implementation risks.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated PMU staffed with experienced procurement and financial management specialists, supported by continuous capacity-building and Bank oversight.
risks.evidence: ADISA is a newly-created agency and the PMU is not yet fully set up, the procurement risk rating is high.

risks.description: The ambitious and compressed reform timeline creates schedule pressure that could lead to implementation delays across multiple agencies.
risks.mitigation: Phase implementation across a five-year horizon, structure results-based financing incentives tied to DLIs through 2020, and provide targeted technical assistance.
risks.evidence: The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk, which is mitigated by the project's span and incentives to deliver up to 2020.

risks.description: Focusing heavily on digital e-services and centralized urban service centers risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and vulnerable populations with limited internet access.
risks.mitigation: Establish assisted digital access points, deploy non-digital information campaigns via grassroots groups, upgrade regional front offices, and monitor usage via user surveys.
risks.evidence: risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable

risks.description: Construction of the Citizen Service Center (CSC) building in Tirana may cause localized environmental impacts including dust, noise, waste, and worker safety hazards.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the Environmental Management Plan (EMP) as part of bidding and construction contracts, conduct regular site monitoring, and maintain regulatory permit compliance.
risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts that are associated with new construction include dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery on site

risks.description: Reforming administrative services across more than ten government agencies presents significant inter-agency coordination challenges.
risks.mitigation: Utilize governance bodies including the Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee, Project Steering Committee, and Prime Minister's Delivery Unit to align agency activities.
risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

risks.description: Civil servants and line agency managers may resist surrendering front-office responsibilities or changing entrenched administrative workflows.
risks.mitigation: Deploy a dedicated change management and communication program, engage key reform champions early, and align institutional performance incentives.
risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions.

risks.description: Ongoing operation, maintenance, and software licensing costs for new IT systems and CSC facilities could impose long-term financial sustainability challenges.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate system lifecycle and maintenance costs into long-term budget planning, offset by operational efficiency gains achieved through business process re-engineering.
risks.evidence: Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance.

risks.description: Incomplete legacy database digitization, missing ID numbers, and legal title disputes at IPRO could delay automated service delivery.
risks.mitigation: Re-engineer business processes, mandate National ID integration, and connect agency databases to the Government Interoperability Platform.
risks.evidence: National ID number is missing for most records, only 45 to 50 percent of the archive is digitized, and legal issues over ownership remain

risks.description: Failure to complete global prerequisite DLI #5 (Reform Policy Document approval and baseline survey) would prevent all RBF loan disbursements.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize and fast-track the Reform Policy Document approval and baseline survey completion during project preparation using PPF funds.
risks.evidence: This is a “global” DLI, which means that no disbursements under the RBF component will be made until DLI#5 is met.

risks.description: Manual payroll systems and fragmented controls across participating agencies create risks of error in reporting Eligible Expenditure Programs (EEPs).
risks.mitigation: Conduct internal audits on payroll linkages, enforce dual signatures, and accelerate integration with the national HRMIS.
risks.evidence: payroll systems remain by and large manual systems, and the associated controls are manually based as well. System cannot communicate with each other.

risks.description: Inadequate financial management software and lack of donor-project experience at ADISA could cause delays in financial reporting and audit compliance.
risks.mitigation: Recruit two finance specialists, procure dedicated accounting software during the PPF phase, and adopt a detailed Financial Management Manual.
risks.evidence: Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations, therefore capacity strengthening would be recommended

risks.description: Failure to achieve and verify agreed Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) will result in withheld loan disbursements under the Results-Based Financing component.
risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance for business process re-engineering, software deployment, and front-office upgrades, backed by third-party verification.
risks.evidence: Where achievement of a DLI cannot be verified, an amount equivalent to the price of that DLI will be withheld.
